criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Clear motivation, users (marine/conservation scientists) and functions identified with cited literature. However, no explicit mission objectives, quantitative requirements (resolution, revisit, coverage) or feasibility discussion of the seafloor-colour sensing concept, so not fully accomplished.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.
Reef-monitoring satellites could also be used to report sea surface temperatures, thermal stress on coral, and bathymetry

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Detailed week-by-week Gantt chart with task descriptions tied to mission needs (launch, orbit, ground control, comms) and a sources list. Plan is credible and feasible, but no contingency/variation provisions and no justification of schedule risks, so not accomplished.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart. Detailed task descriptions can be found on the next page.
The goal is to brainstorm and research as many possible strategies for the satellite’s launch/orbit and then gradually cut and refine them

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Progress is limited to background reading, mission concept drafting and STK tutorials. No preliminary technical results (orbit parameters, coverage, link budgets, hand calculations) or interpretation are presented, so only minor work is demonstrated.

evidence.quote: I have read the brief of Asner’s monitoring system in Hawaii, researched into how coral bleaching occurs and its severity

criteria.reasoning: Well-written, logically structured with clear headings, consistent formatting, labelled Gantt chart with legend, and footnote citations matching listed sources. Minor weakness: the 'Useful Links' list is not cited in text, preventing a higher mark.

technical_issues.issue: No quantitative mission requirements (spatial resolution, revisit time, swath, spectral bands) despite citing 100 m/pixel bathymetry gap; seafloor-colour bleaching detection implies demanding high-resolution multispectral imaging not yet addressed.
No preliminary orbit or coverage analysis performed; near-real-time relay claim is unquantified (LEO revisit vs GEO trade-off not discussed).
Gantt chart shows 'STK Simulations' spanning Wk 4–10 but no simulation outputs are reported, inconsistent with claimed progress.

overall: A well-presented, clearly written preliminary report with a compelling Australian reef-monitoring mission concept, a detailed Gantt-chart plan and cited sources. Weaknesses: no formal mission requirements, no contingency planning, and preliminary progress limited to tutorials with no technical results.

feedback.summary: Your preliminary report presents a compelling Australian reef-monitoring mission with clear motivation, identified users, a detailed week-by-week Gantt chart and cited sources. Presentation is strong. To reach the top rubric levels, you need quantitative mission requirements, contingency planning in your schedule, and preliminary technical results — such as orbit or coverage analysis — rather than progress limited to tutorials and background reading.
next_steps: Define quantitative mission requirements (spatial resolution, revisit time, swath, spectral bands) and link each to user needs, then discuss feasibility of seafloor-colour bleaching detection.
Add contingency provisions to your Gantt chart (e.g., buffer weeks, fallback strategies for launch/orbit trade-offs) and justify schedule risks in the context of the mission.

Produce and interpret at least one preliminary technical result in STK — e.g., a candidate orbit with coverage/revisit analysis — to substantiate the 'STK Simulations' weeks 4–10 plan and your near-real-time relay claim.

criteria.C1: Your Mission Concept & Rationale clearly motivates the mission, identifies marine and conservation scientists as users, and cites relevant literature (e.g., Asner's Hawaii system). To reach Accomplished, state explicit mission objectives and quantitative requirements — resolution, revisit time, coverage, spectral bands — and discuss feasibility of detecting seafloor-colour bleaching, since this implies demanding high-resolution multispectral imaging you have not yet addressed.
criteria.C2: Your week-by-week Gantt chart with task descriptions tied to mission needs (launch, orbit, ground control, comms) and your sources list make the plan credible and feasible. For Accomplished, add provisions for variations and contingencies — schedule buffers, fallback options — and explain why the plan is structured this way in the context of the mission, including schedule risks such as the STK Simulations block spanning weeks 4–10.
criteria.C3: Your progress so far — background reading, concept drafting and STK tutorials 1–4 — demonstrates only minor work. The Accomplished level requires a good preliminary set of results with brief interpretation: for example, candidate orbit parameters, coverage or revisit calculations, or link-budget hand calculations. Note your Gantt chart plans simulations but no simulation outputs are reported yet, which is inconsistent with the claimed progress.
criteria.C4: Your report is well-written, logically structured with clear headings, consistent formatting, a labelled Gantt chart with legend, and footnote citations matching your reference list — well done. The one barrier to a higher mark is the 'Useful Links' section, which is not cited in the text. Integrate those sources into the body with proper in-text citations so all listed references are matched in both directions.
